questions.q: When a validation rule's Error Condition Formula evaluates to TRUE, what happens?
options: The record is saved and an email alert fires
Salesforce blocks the save and shows the Error Message
The record is routed into an approval process
Nothing; TRUE means the data is valid
questions.explain: A validation rule's formula describes invalid data. TRUE means the data violates the rule, so the save is blocked and the error message shown.

questions.q: What does the formula LEN(AccountNumber) <> 8 actually check for?
options: That Account Number is exactly 8 characters long, blocking the save when it is not
That Account Number is blank
That Account Number contains only numbers
That Account Number equals the literal text "8"
questions.explain: The formula is TRUE when the length is NOT 8, which blocks the save, which is how it enforces an 8-character account number.

questions.q: Which field on a validation rule determines what the user sees when their save is blocked?
options: Rule Name
Error Location
Error Message
Active checkbox
questions.explain: Error Message is the text shown to the user. Error Location controls where on the page it appears, not what it says.

questions.q: Which function checks whether a field has no value at all?
options: LEN()
ISBLANK()
AND()
NOT()
questions.explain: ISBLANK(field) returns true when the field is empty, commonly combined with AND or OR in a larger validation formula.

questions.q: When does a validation rule run on a record?
options: Only the very first time the record is ever saved
Only when an approval process is also active on the object
On every save, insert or update, for as long as the rule is active
Only when a user manually clicks Check Syntax
questions.explain: A validation rule is a standing gate: it fires on every insert and update while active, not just once.
